lessons.title: Shopping for Groceries
lessons.description: In this lesson, learners will read about a shopping trip and practice finding specific details about items and prices. They will also learn to understand the main idea of a short text.

sections.heading: Finding the Main Idea
sections.content: The main idea is the most important point the writer wants to tell you. It often answers the question 'What is this text mostly about?' Look at the first and last sentences, or repeated words, to help you find it.

sections.heading: Scanning for Details
sections.content: When you need to find specific information like a name, a number, or a price, you don't need to read every word. Move your eyes quickly over the text until you see the keywords related to your question. This is called scanning.

sections.heading: Vocabulary in Context
sections.content: Sometimes you don't know a word, but you can guess its meaning from the other words around it. For example, if a text says 'The apples were fresh and juicy,' you can guess 'juicy' means they have a lot of liquid, even if you don't know the word exactly.

passage.title: My Trip to the Supermarket
passage.content: Yesterday, I went to the supermarket near my house. I needed to buy some food for the week. First, I bought some fresh vegetables: tomatoes, carrots, and a big cabbage. The tomatoes were 20,000 VND per kilo. Then, I went to the fruit section. I chose some sweet oranges and ripe bananas. The bananas cost 15,000 VND for a bunch. I also bought a carton of milk and a loaf of bread. The milk was 30,000 VND and the bread was 12,000 VND. Finally, I paid at the checkout. The total bill was 125,000 VND. It was a good shopping trip, and now my fridge is full!

questions.stemText: What is the main idea of this text?
options: The writer likes to eat fruit.
The writer went shopping for food.
The supermarket is near the writer's house.
The writer spent too much money.

questions.stemText: What did the writer buy first?
How much did the bananas cost?
What other item did the writer buy from the dairy section?
What was the total cost of the shopping trip?
Which word means 'ready to eat' for fruit?
What does 'checkout' mean in the text?
options: The place where you pay for your items.
The place where you find vegetables.
The place where you leave the supermarket.
The place where you return items.

questions.stemText: How does the writer feel after shopping?
options: Happy because the fridge is full

lessons.title: A Day Trip to Ho Chi Minh City
lessons.description: Learners will read about a visit to a big city and practice identifying the sequence of events and understanding specific details about places and activities.

sections.heading: Understanding Sequence of Events
sections.content: When a text describes a trip or a series of actions, look for words like 'first,' 'then,' 'next,' 'after that,' and 'finally.' These words help you understand the order in which things happened. This is important for following a story or instructions.

sections.heading: Identifying Key Information
sections.content: Not all information in a text is equally important. Focus on the 'who,' 'what,' 'where,' 'when,' and 'why' of the story. These are often the key facts you need to remember or answer questions about. Practice picking out these main points.

sections.heading: Guessing Meaning from Context
sections.content: If you see a word like 'landmarks' and the text talks about 'famous buildings like the Opera House and Notre Dame Cathedral,' you can guess that 'landmarks' means important and well-known places or buildings in a city. Use the surrounding words to help you understand.

passage.title: My Exciting Day in Ho Chi Minh City
passage.content: Last Saturday, my family and I took a bus to Ho Chi Minh City for a day trip. First, we visited Ben Thanh Market. It was very busy, and we saw many beautiful souvenirs and tried some delicious street food. Then, we walked to the Notre Dame Cathedral and the Central Post Office. These are famous landmarks, and we took many photos there. After that, we had lunch at a nice restaurant with traditional Vietnamese food. In the afternoon, we went to a big shopping mall. My sister bought a new shirt. Finally, before going home, we enjoyed some cool drinks at a cafe. It was a long but wonderful day, and I want to visit again soon!

questions.stemText: What was the first place the family visited in Ho Chi Minh City?
What did they do at Ben Thanh Market?
options: Saw souvenirs and tried street food

questions.stemText: Which two famous landmarks did they visit after the market?
options: Ben Thanh Market and a shopping mall
Notre Dame Cathedral and the Central Post Office
The Opera House and a museum

questions.stemText: What kind of food did they eat for lunch?
What did the sister buy at the shopping mall?
What does 'landmarks' mean in the text?
How did the family travel to Ho Chi Minh City?
How did the writer feel about the day trip?
options: Excited and wanting to go again

lessons.title: My Favorite Hobbies
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners understand personal preferences and specific details about hobbies. They will practice identifying key information and understanding why someone enjoys an activity.

sections.heading: Identifying Specific Information
sections.content: When reading about someone's interests or preferences, look for details that answer 'what,' 'how often,' 'where,' and 'why.' These specific pieces of information help you build a clear picture of the topic. Don't just read; actively look for these facts.

sections.heading: Understanding Preferences
sections.content: Authors often use words like 'love,' 'enjoy,' 'like,' 'favorite,' or 'find it relaxing/interesting' to show what they prefer. Pay attention to these words to understand the writer's feelings about a topic. This helps you grasp their main point.

sections.heading: Inferring Information
sections.content: Sometimes the text doesn't directly tell you something, but you can guess it. If someone says 'I spend hours in my garden, watching my flowers grow,' you can infer that gardening makes them feel calm and happy, even if they don't say 'gardening makes me happy'.

passage.title: What I Love to Do in My Free Time
passage.content: I have two favorite hobbies that I really enjoy. First, I love reading books. I usually read for an hour every evening before bed. I like many kinds of books, especially adventure stories and detective novels. Reading helps me relax and learn new things. My second hobby is playing badminton. I play with my friends at the local park every Saturday morning. We usually play for about two hours. It's a great way to stay active and have fun together. I feel happy and energetic after playing. Sometimes, if the weather is bad, I watch films at home instead. Hobbies are important because they help us relax and enjoy life.

questions.stemText: What are the writer's two favorite hobbies?
How often does the writer read books?
options: Only when the weather is bad

questions.stemText: What kind of books does the writer especially like?
Where does the writer play badminton?
How long do they usually play badminton?
What does 'energetic' mean in the text?
What does the writer do if the weather is bad?
Why does the writer think hobbies are important?
options: They help us relax and enjoy life.
They help us finish school work.

lessons.title: My Job as a Teacher
lessons.description: This lesson focuses on understanding descriptions of jobs and workplaces. Learners will practice identifying specific tasks and the environment of a job.

sections.heading: Understanding Job Descriptions
sections.content: When reading about a job, pay attention to what the person does, where they work, and what skills or qualities are mentioned. These details help you understand the nature of the job. Look for verbs that describe actions and nouns that describe places or tools.

sections.heading: Matching Information
sections.content: Some questions ask you to match a task with a specific part of the job or a place with an activity. Read the question carefully and then scan the text for keywords from both parts of the question. This helps you find the correct connection quickly.

sections.heading: Recognizing Workplace Vocabulary
sections.content: Words like 'office,' 'school,' 'hospital,' 'factory,' 'colleagues,' 'students,' 'patients' are common in texts about jobs. Knowing these words helps you quickly understand the context. If you see 'students' and 'classroom,' you know the job is likely teaching.

passage.title: A Day in My Life as a Teacher
passage.content: My name is Mai, and I am an English teacher at a primary school in Hanoi. I love my job because I enjoy helping young children learn. My workplace is a bright and colorful classroom. Every morning, I prepare my lessons and activities. From 8 AM to 4 PM, I teach different classes. I help students with reading, writing, and speaking English. We often play games and sing songs to make learning fun. I also talk to parents about their children's progress. My colleagues are very friendly, and we often share ideas. Being a teacher can be challenging, but it is also very rewarding when I see my students improve.

questions.stemText: What is Mai's job?
Where does Mai work?
What does Mai do every morning?
What subjects does Mai help students with?
How does Mai make learning fun?
options: By giving a lot of homework
By playing games and singing songs

questions.stemText: What does 'colleagues' mean in the text?
How does Mai feel about her job?
What time does Mai finish teaching classes?

lessons.title: Tips for Staying Healthy
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners understand advice related to health. They will practice identifying key recommendations and understanding the benefits of healthy habits.

sections.heading: Identifying Advice and Recommendations
sections.content: When reading texts that give advice, look for words like 'should,' 'must,' 'try to,' 'it's important to,' or phrases that suggest a good idea. These signal that the writer is giving a recommendation. Pay attention to the main points of advice.

sections.heading: Understanding Benefits
sections.content: Often, advice is followed by an explanation of why it's good. Look for phrases like 'because,' 'so that,' 'this helps you,' or 'it's good for.' Understanding the benefits helps you remember the advice and its purpose. Connect the action to its positive result.

sections.heading: Recognizing Health Vocabulary
sections.content: Words like 'exercise,' 'balanced diet,' 'sleep,' 'water,' 'stress,' 'vitamins' are common in health texts. Familiarize yourself with these terms. If you see 'eat five portions of fruit and vegetables,' you can infer this is part of a 'balanced diet'.

passage.title: My Daily Routine for a Healthy Life
passage.content: Staying healthy is very important for a happy life. I try to follow a few simple rules every day. First, I always eat a balanced diet. This means I eat a lot of fresh fruits and vegetables, some rice, and lean protein like chicken or fish. I try to avoid too much sugar and fast food. Second, I exercise regularly. I go jogging in the park three times a week for 30 minutes. Exercise makes my body strong and helps me feel good. Third, I make sure to get enough sleep, about 7-8 hours every night. Good sleep helps my brain work well. Finally, I drink plenty of water throughout the day. These habits help me stay active and healthy.

questions.stemText: What is the main idea of the text?
options: The writer shares tips for staying healthy.
The writer eats a lot of fruit.
The writer sleeps 7-8 hours every night.

questions.stemText: What does a 'balanced diet' mean for the writer?
options: Eating a lot of sugar and fast food
Eating fresh fruits, vegetables, rice, and lean protein

questions.stemText: How often does the writer go jogging?
How long does the writer jog for each time?
How many hours of sleep does the writer try to get?
What does 'plenty of water' mean?
What does exercise help the writer do?
options: Make their body strong and feel good

questions.stemText: What does good sleep help with?

lessons.title: My Favorite Sport: Football
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners understand details about a sport and its benefits. They will practice identifying specific information and understanding the reasons for enjoying an activity.

sections.heading: Identifying Key Details
sections.content: When reading about a sport or activity, look for specific details like the name of the sport, where it's played, who plays it, what equipment is needed, and how often it's done. These details give you a complete picture of the activity. Use these details to answer 'who, what, where, when, why, how' questions.

sections.heading: Understanding Benefits of Activities
sections.content: Many texts explain why an activity is good. Look for words and phrases that describe positive outcomes, such as 'helps me relax,' 'keeps me fit,' 'good for teamwork,' or 'makes me happy.' Connecting the activity to its benefits helps you understand the writer's perspective.

sections.heading: Vocabulary for Sports
sections.content: Common sports vocabulary includes 'team,' 'player,' 'ball,' 'field,' 'court,' 'score,' 'win,' 'lose,' 'practice,' 'exercise.' If you see 'kick the ball' and 'score a goal,' you can guess the sport is football, even if it's not explicitly stated at first.

passage.title: My Passion for Football
passage.content: Football is my favorite sport, and I play it every Sunday morning with my friends. We meet at the local stadium near our houses. We usually play for about two hours. I love football because it's exciting, and it helps me stay fit and strong. You need a ball, a field, and two teams to play. Each team tries to kick the ball into the other team's goal to score points. It's a great way to exercise and also to work as a team. After the game, we are often tired but very happy. Sometimes, we watch professional football matches on TV together. I dream of playing for a big team one day!

questions.stemText: What is the writer's favorite sport?
When does the writer play football?
Where do they play football?
What do you need to play football?
options: A ball, a field, and two teams
A swimming pool and a cap

questions.stemText: What is the main goal in football?
options: To kick the ball into the other team's goal

questions.stemText: What does 'stay fit' mean in the text?
options: To be good at watching TV

questions.stemText: How do the players feel after the game?
What does the writer dream of?

lessons.title: My Trip to the History Museum
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners understand descriptions of places and specific exhibits in a museum. They will practice identifying key information and understanding what someone learned.

sections.heading: Understanding Descriptions of Places
sections.content: When reading about a place like a museum, look for words that describe its size, atmosphere, and what kind of things you can see there. Adjectives are very helpful (e.g., 'big,' 'interesting,' 'old'). These details help you imagine the place.

sections.heading: Identifying Specific Exhibits
sections.content: Museums have different sections or exhibits. Pay attention to names of rooms, types of objects, or historical periods mentioned. Questions often ask about what was seen in a particular part of the museum. Scan for these specific names or categories.

sections.heading: Inferring Learning Outcomes
sections.content: If a text says 'I learned about ancient tools and clothes,' you can infer that the museum helped the person understand how people lived in the past. Look for phrases like 'I learned,' 'it showed me,' or 'I discovered' to understand what new knowledge was gained.

passage.title: A Fascinating Day at the Museum
passage.content: Last Sunday, my class went on a field trip to the National History Museum in Hanoi. It was a very big and interesting place. First, we saw many ancient objects from thousands of years ago, like old pottery and tools. Our guide told us stories about how people lived in the past. Then, we went to a room with traditional Vietnamese clothes. They were so colorful and beautiful! I learned a lot about the history of our country. There was also a special exhibition about famous historical figures. We spent about three hours there. It was a great experience, and I want to go back with my family next time.

questions.stemText: What kind of museum did the class visit?
Where is this museum located?
What did they see first at the museum?
options: Ancient objects like pottery and tools

questions.stemText: Who told them stories about the past?
What did the writer learn a lot about?
What does 'ancient' mean in the text?
How long did they spend at the museum?
How did the writer feel about the visit?

lessons.title: Celebrating Tet Holiday
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners understand cultural traditions, specifically the Tet holiday in Vietnam. They will practice identifying key elements of a tradition and understanding related activities.

sections.heading: Understanding Cultural Traditions
sections.content: When reading about traditions, look for details about when and how they are celebrated, what special foods are eaten, and what activities people do. These elements define a tradition. Pay attention to the sequence of events and the feelings associated with the tradition.

sections.heading: Identifying Key Elements
sections.content: For traditions, key elements often include dates, special clothing, specific foods, family gatherings, and unique customs. Scan the text for these categories of information. For example, if the question is about food, look for food names.

sections.heading: Vocabulary for Celebrations
sections.content: Words like 'celebrate,' 'holiday,' 'tradition,' 'family gathering,' 'decorate,' 'lucky money,' 'fireworks,' 'special food' are common when talking about holidays. Knowing these helps you understand the context. If you read 'lucky money,' you know it's a gift given during a special occasion.

passage.title: Our Family's Tet Celebration
passage.content: Tet, or Lunar New Year, is the most important holiday in Vietnam. My family loves celebrating it! A few days before Tet, we clean and decorate our house. We buy peach blossoms and kumquat trees to make our home beautiful and lucky. On Tet Eve, we have a big family dinner with special traditional dishes like Banh Chung and spring rolls. It's a time for all relatives to gather. Children receive 'lucky money' in red envelopes from adults. During Tet, we visit grandparents and other family members. We wear new clothes and wish each other good health and happiness. Tet is a wonderful time for family, food, and new beginnings.

questions.stemText: What is Tet also known as?
What do families do a few days before Tet?
What special trees do they buy for decoration?
What is a traditional dish mentioned for Tet dinner?
What do children receive from adults during Tet?
What does 'relatives' mean in the text?
What do people wish each other during Tet?
What is the overall feeling of Tet for the writer?
options: A time for family, food, and new beginnings

lessons.title: Making a New Friend at School
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners understand social interactions and the process of making new friends. They will practice identifying key events and understanding reasons for actions.

sections.heading: Understanding Social Interactions
sections.content: When reading about people meeting, pay attention to who starts the conversation, what they talk about, and what activities they do together. These details show how a relationship develops. Look for dialogue and descriptions of actions.

sections.heading: Identifying Reasons for Actions
sections.content: People do things for reasons. Look for words like 'because,' 'so,' 'to,' or phrases that explain 'why.' For example, if someone 'smiled because she was friendly,' you understand the reason for her action. This helps with inference.

sections.heading: Vocabulary for Friendship
sections.content: Words like 'friendly,' 'talk,' 'share,' 'laugh,' 'play together,' 'become friends,' 'introduce' are common when talking about making friends. If a text says 'we talked for a long time and found many common interests,' you can infer they are becoming friends.

passage.title: My New Friend, Linh
passage.content: Last month, a new girl named Linh joined my class. She was a bit shy at first, sitting alone during break time. I felt a little nervous, but I decided to say hello. I walked over to her and asked, 'Hi, I'm An. Do you want to play skipping rope with us?' She smiled and said, 'Yes, please!' We started playing, and soon she was laughing with everyone. After that, we talked about our favorite subjects and hobbies. We found out we both love drawing and reading adventure books. Now, Linh and I always sit together at lunch and help each other with homework. I'm so happy to have a new friend!

questions.stemText: Who is the new girl in the class?
How did Linh seem at first?
What did An ask Linh to do first?
What did An and Linh find out they both love?
What do Linh and An do together now?
options: Sit together at lunch and help with homework

questions.stemText: What does 'nervous' mean in the text?
options: Feeling a little worried or scared

questions.stemText: How did Linh react when An invited her to play?
How does An feel about having Linh as a friend?

lessons.title: Taking the Bus to School
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners understand how to use public transport. They will practice identifying the sequence of actions and specific details about a journey.

sections.heading: Understanding Instructions and Sequence
sections.content: When reading about a process, like taking public transport, pay close attention to the order of actions. Look for words like 'first,' 'then,' 'next,' 'after that,' and 'finally.' These words help you follow the steps correctly and understand the journey.

sections.heading: Identifying Key Information for Travel
sections.content: For travel texts, focus on details like the type of transport, the starting point, the destination, how to pay, and any specific instructions. These are often tested in comprehension questions. Scan for names of places, numbers, and verbs related to travel.

sections.heading: Vocabulary for Public Transport
sections.content: Words like 'bus stop,' 'bus ticket,' 'fare,' 'route,' 'destination,' 'get on,' 'get off,' 'conductor,' 'schedule' are common. If you read 'I waited at the bus stop for bus number 10,' you know the person is using a bus.

passage.title: My Daily Bus Journey
passage.content: Every morning, I take the bus to school. It's a convenient and cheap way to travel. First, I walk to the bus stop near my house. I usually arrive at 6:45 AM and wait for bus number 15. The bus usually comes at 6:55 AM. When the bus arrives, I get on and show my student bus card to the driver. The bus is often full of other students and people going to work. I try to find a seat, but sometimes I have to stand. The journey to school takes about 20 minutes. I get off at the stop right in front of my school. It's a good system, and I always arrive on time for my first class.

questions.stemText: What kind of public transport does the writer use?
Where does the writer wait for the bus?
options: At the bus stop near their house

questions.stemText: What time does the writer usually arrive at the bus stop?
What does the writer show to the driver?
How long does the journey to school take?
What does 'convenient' mean in the text?
Who else is often on the bus?
options: Other students and people going to work

questions.stemText: How does the writer feel about arriving at school?

lessons.title: Cooking My Favorite Dish
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners understand a simple cooking process. They will practice identifying ingredients, steps, and understanding the outcome of a recipe.

sections.heading: Understanding Steps in a Process
sections.content: When reading a recipe or instructions, it's important to follow the steps in order. Look for numbers, bullet points, or sequence words like 'first,' 'then,' 'next,' and 'finally.' Each step builds on the last one, so understanding the order is key.

sections.heading: Identifying Ingredients
sections.content: Recipes always list the things you need to cook. Scan the text for names of food items, spices, and liquids. These are your ingredients. Make a mental list or quickly note them down if you need to answer specific questions about what is used.

sections.heading: Vocabulary for Cooking
sections.content: Words like 'chop,' 'mix,' 'fry,' 'boil,' 'add,' 'ingredients,' 'recipe,' 'dish,' 'serve' are common in cooking texts. If you read 'chop the onions and garlic,' you know these items need to be cut into small pieces.

passage.title: How I Make Simple Fried Rice
passage.content: My favorite dish to cook at home is simple fried rice. It's quick, easy, and delicious! First, I chop some onions, garlic, and carrots into small pieces. I also prepare some cooked rice and a few eggs. Next, I heat a little oil in a pan. I add the chopped onions and garlic and fry them until they smell good. Then, I add the carrots and cook them for a few minutes. After that, I push the vegetables to one side, crack the eggs into the pan, and scramble them. Finally, I add the cooked rice, a little soy sauce, and mix everything together. I stir-fry it for a few more minutes until it's hot. I love to eat it with some fresh cucumber.

questions.stemText: What is the writer's favorite dish to cook?
What are the first three vegetables the writer chops?
What does the writer add to the pan after the onions and garlic?
What does the writer do with the eggs?
What liquid ingredient is added at the end with the rice?
What does 'chop' mean in the text?
How does the writer like to eat the fried rice?
What is the overall feeling about cooking this dish?

lessons.title: My Favorite Film: 'Coco'
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners understand descriptions of films and personal preferences. They will practice identifying key plot points and reasons for liking a film.

sections.heading: Understanding Film Descriptions
sections.content: When reading about a film, look for its title, genre (e.g., animation, action, comedy), main characters, and a brief summary of the story. Pay attention to words that describe the film's mood or message. This helps you understand what the film is about.

sections.heading: Identifying Reasons for Preference
sections.content: Authors often explain why they like something. Look for phrases like 'I love it because,' 'the best part is,' 'it makes me feel,' or 'it teaches me.' These phrases directly tell you the reasons for their preference. Connect these reasons to the film's qualities.

sections.heading: Vocabulary for Films
sections.content: Words like 'character,' 'story,' 'plot,' 'director,' 'actor,' 'animation,' 'soundtrack,' 'message,' 'emotional,' 'funny' are common. If a text says 'the main character wants to be a musician,' you know who the story is mostly about.

passage.title: Why I Love the Film 'Coco'
passage.content: My favorite film is 'Coco.' It's an animated musical fantasy film from Disney Pixar. The story is about a young boy named Miguel who loves music, but his family hates it because of an old family history. Miguel dreams of becoming a famous musician like his idol, Ernesto de la Cruz. On the Day of the Dead, he accidentally enters the Land of the Dead. There, he meets his ancestors and tries to find his great-great-grandfather to get their blessing for his music. I love this film because the animation is beautiful, the songs are amazing, and it has a wonderful message about family, memory, and following your dreams. It always makes me feel happy and a little bit sad at the same time.

questions.stemText: What kind of film is 'Coco'?
Who is the main character of the film?
What does Miguel dream of becoming?
Where does Miguel accidentally go?
options: To the Land of the Dead

questions.stemText: What is one reason the writer loves the film?
options: The beautiful animation and amazing songs

questions.stemText: What does 'ancestors' mean in the text?
What is one message of the film?
options: About family, memory, and following your dreams

questions.stemText: How does the film make the writer feel?
options: Happy and a little bit sad at the same time

lessons.title: Joining the School Art Club
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners understand descriptions of school clubs. They will practice identifying the purpose, activities, and schedule of a club.

sections.heading: Identifying Purpose and Activities
sections.content: When reading about a club or organization, look for what its main goal is and what members actually do. The purpose explains 'why' the club exists, and the activities explain 'what' happens during meetings. These are key to understanding the club.

sections.heading: Understanding Schedules and Logistics
sections.content: Clubs often have specific meeting times, days, and locations. Scan the text for this logistical information. Questions might ask about when or where the club meets, or how often. Keywords like 'every,' 'on,' 'at,' 'from' are useful.

sections.heading: Vocabulary for School Clubs
sections.content: Words like 'club,' 'member,' 'join,' 'meet,' 'activity,' 'project,' 'practice,' 'learn,' 'skill,' 'creative' are common. If a text says 'we learn to paint and draw,' you can infer it's an art-related club.

passage.title: My Favorite School Club
passage.content: I am a member of the Art Club at my school, and it's my favorite activity! We meet every Tuesday afternoon from 3:30 PM to 5:00 PM in the art classroom. Our club has about 15 students who love to draw, paint, and create things. In the club, we learn different art techniques, like how to use watercolors, pencils, and clay. Sometimes, we work on individual projects, and other times we work together on a big mural for the school. Our teacher, Ms. Hoa, is very kind and helps us with new ideas. I love the Art Club because it helps me be creative and relax after a long day of classes. Plus, I've made many new friends there who share my passion for art.

questions.stemText: What club is the writer a member of?
When does the club meet?
Where does the club meet?
What do members learn to use in the club?
What is one type of project they work on together?
options: A big mural for the school

questions.stemText: What does 'creative' mean in the text?
options: To be good at making new things or having new ideas

questions.stemText: Who helps the students with new ideas?
Why does the writer love the Art Club?
options: It helps them be creative and relax.
It helps them get good grades.

lessons.title: A Weekend Trip to Da Lat
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners understand travel plans and activities during a trip. They will practice identifying key details about a destination and what people did there.

sections.heading: Understanding Travel Plans
sections.content: When reading about a trip, look for information about the destination, how the people traveled, who they went with, and how long they stayed. These details give you the basic framework of the journey. Pay attention to names of places and modes of transport.

sections.heading: Identifying Activities During a Trip
sections.content: A trip usually involves many activities. Scan the text for verbs that describe what people did (e.g., 'visited,' 'walked,' 'ate,' 'saw'). These actions tell you about their experiences at the destination. Make a mental list of the main things they did.

sections.heading: Vocabulary for Travel
sections.content: Words like 'destination,' 'journey,' 'explore,' 'sightseeing,' 'souvenirs,' 'scenery,' 'relax,' 'trip,' 'hotel' are common in travel texts. If you read 'we enjoyed the cool weather and beautiful scenery,' you understand the natural beauty of the place.

passage.title: My Wonderful Weekend in Da Lat
passage.content: Last weekend, my family and I took a short trip to Da Lat. We traveled by bus, and the journey took about six hours. Da Lat is famous for its cool weather, beautiful flowers, and pine forests. On Saturday, we visited the Valley of Love, where we took many pictures of the colorful gardens. We also went to the Da Lat Market and bought some fresh local fruits like strawberries. For dinner, we tried some delicious local food. On Sunday morning, we explored Xuan Huong Lake by paddle boat. It was very peaceful. Before heading home, we bought some souvenirs. It was a relaxing and memorable trip. I love the fresh air and quiet atmosphere of Da Lat.

questions.stemText: Where did the writer and their family go for the weekend trip?
How did they travel to Da Lat?
What is Da Lat famous for?
options: Cool weather, beautiful flowers, and pine forests

questions.stemText: What did they do at the Valley of Love?
options: Took many pictures of colorful gardens

questions.stemText: What kind of fruit did they buy at Da Lat Market?
What does 'scenery' mean in the text?
options: The natural features of a landscape

questions.stemText: How did they explore Xuan Huong Lake?
How does the writer describe the trip?

lessons.title: How I Use the Internet
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners understand the various uses of the internet in daily life. They will practice identifying different online activities and their benefits.

sections.heading: Understanding Uses of Technology
sections.content: When reading about technology like the internet, look for the different ways people use it. These can be for work, study, entertainment, or communication. Pay attention to verbs that describe online actions (e.g., 'search,' 'watch,' 'chat,' 'buy').

sections.heading: Identifying Benefits and Purposes
sections.content: For each use of the internet, there's usually a reason or benefit. Look for phrases that explain 'why' someone uses it in a particular way (e.g., 'to find information,' 'to connect with friends,' 'to relax'). This helps you understand the value of each activity.

sections.heading: Vocabulary for the Internet
sections.content: Words like 'online,' 'website,' 'email,' 'social media,' 'video call,' 'search engine,' 'download,' 'upload,' 'information,' 'entertainment' are common. If you read 'I send emails to my teacher,' you know it's a way to communicate digitally.

passage.title: My Digital Life: The Internet
passage.content: The internet is a big part of my daily life. I use it for many things, both for school and for fun. For school, I often use a search engine to find information for my projects. I also watch educational videos on YouTube to understand difficult topics. Sometimes, I send emails to my teachers if I have questions about homework. For fun, I use social media to chat with my friends and share photos. I also love watching films and TV shows on streaming platforms. Sometimes, I play online games with friends. The internet helps me learn, stay connected with people, and relax. It's an amazing tool, but it's important to use it wisely and not spend too much time online.

questions.stemText: What is the main idea of the text?
options: The writer only uses the internet for school.
The writer talks about how they use the internet for many things.
The writer spends too much time online.
The writer only uses social media.

questions.stemText: How does the writer find information for school projects?
What kind of videos does the writer watch on YouTube for school?
How does the writer communicate with teachers about homework questions?
What does the writer use social media for?
options: To chat with friends and share photos

questions.stemText: What does 'streaming platforms' mean in the text?
options: Websites for watching films and TV shows

questions.stemText: What are two benefits of the internet mentioned by the writer?
options: It helps them sleep and eat.
It helps them learn and stay connected with people.
It helps them make money and travel.
It helps them clean their house and cook.

questions.stemText: What advice does the writer give about using the internet?
options: Use it wisely and not too much.

lessons.title: A Letter from My Pen Pal, Tom
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners understand personal letters and infer information about a person. They will practice identifying personal details and understanding the purpose of a letter.

sections.heading: Understanding Personal Letters
sections.content: Personal letters usually start with a greeting (e.g., 'Dear [Name]') and end with a closing (e.g., 'Best regards,' 'Sincerely'). The body of the letter contains personal news, questions, and descriptions of daily life or interests. Look for these common features.

sections.heading: Identifying Personal Information
sections.content: When reading a letter from a new person, pay attention to details about their name, age, where they live, their family, hobbies, and school. These facts help you get to know the writer. Scan for nouns and adjectives that describe these aspects.

sections.heading: Inferring Feelings and Intentions
sections.content: Sometimes a letter doesn't directly say 'I am happy,' but you can infer it from phrases like 'I had a great time' or 'I'm excited to hear from you.' Also, look for questions to understand what the writer wants to know from you. This helps you understand the person better.

passage.title: Hello from England!
passage.content:
Dear Lan,

Hello from England! My name is Tom, and I'm 14 years old. I live in a small town near London with my parents and my younger sister, Lily. I was so happy to get your first letter! Thank you for telling me about your life in Vietnam. It sounds very interesting.

I go to a secondary school here. My favorite subjects are History and Science. After school, I love playing football with my friends in the park. On weekends, I often read adventure books or watch films. Sometimes, my family and I go for walks in the countryside.

What about your school? What are your favorite subjects? Do you have any pets? I have a cat named Whiskers. She is very playful. I'm looking forward to hearing from you soon!

Best wishes,
Tom

questions.stemText: Where does Tom live?
options: In a big city in England
In a small town near London

questions.stemText: How old is Tom?
Who does Tom live with?
What are Tom's favorite subjects at school?
What does Tom do after school?
What is the name of Tom's pet?
What does Tom ask Lan about her school?
options: How many students are in her class
If she has a school uniform

questions.stemText: What does 'looking forward to hearing from you' mean?
options: He hopes to get another letter soon.
He is busy and cannot write.

lessons.title: A Trip to Our Local Market
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners understand descriptions of local markets. They will practice identifying types of goods, the atmosphere, and specific details about the market.

sections.heading: Understanding Descriptions of Places
sections.content: When reading about a place like a market, look for words that describe what it looks, sounds, and smells like. Pay attention to the types of things sold, the people who are there, and the overall feeling of the place. Adjectives and sensory words are very helpful.

sections.heading: Identifying Types of Goods
sections.content: Markets sell many different items. Scan the text for categories of goods (e.g., 'fresh produce,' 'clothes,' 'handicrafts') and specific examples (e.g., 'vegetables,' 'fish,' 'shirts'). This helps you understand the variety available. Make a mental list of what you can buy.

sections.heading: Vocabulary for Markets
sections.content: Words like 'stall,' 'vendor,' 'bargain,' 'fresh,' 'local,' 'crowded,' 'lively,' 'produce,' 'handicrafts,' 'spices' are common. If you read 'vendors call out their prices,' you know people are selling things and making noise to attract customers.

passage.title: My Morning at the Local Market
passage.content: Every Saturday morning, my mother and I go to the local market. It's not a big supermarket, but a traditional outdoor market. It's always very lively and a bit crowded, full of sounds and smells. First, we visit the vegetable stalls. The farmers sell fresh tomatoes, green leafy vegetables, and herbs. Everything looks so fresh! Then, we go to the meat and fish section. My mother always buys fresh fish for our dinner. There are also stalls selling fruits, like mangoes and dragon fruit, and sometimes even beautiful flowers. I love walking around and seeing all the different things. The vendors are friendly, and sometimes my mother can bargain for a better price. It's a great place to find fresh, local food.

questions.stemText: When do the writer and their mother go to the local market?
What kind of market is it?
What do the farmers sell at the vegetable stalls?
options: Fresh tomatoes, green leafy vegetables, and herbs

questions.stemText: What does the mother always buy from the meat and fish section?
What kind of fruits are mentioned as being sold at the market?
What does 'lively' mean when describing the market?
What can the mother sometimes do with the vendors?
What is the market a great place to find?

lessons.title: Helping Our Environment
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners understand actions to protect nature. They will practice identifying specific ways to help the environment and understanding the importance of these actions.

sections.heading: Identifying Actions and Their Purpose
sections.content: When reading about environmental protection, look for specific actions people take (e.g., 'recycle,' 'save water,' 'plant trees') and the reasons why these actions are important (e.g., 'to reduce waste,' 'to protect animals'). Connect the action to its positive impact.

sections.heading: Understanding Environmental Themes
sections.content: Texts about nature often focus on themes like pollution, conservation, recycling, and sustainability. Familiarize yourself with these concepts. If a text talks about 'plastic bags harming sea animals,' the theme is likely pollution and its impact on wildlife.

sections.heading: Vocabulary for Nature and Environment
sections.content: Words like 'nature,' 'environment,' 'recycle,' 'reduce,' 'reuse,' 'pollution,' 'waste,' 'plant,' 'save energy,' 'protect' are common. If you read 'we collect plastic bottles and paper,' you can infer they are talking about 'recycling'.

passage.title: Small Actions, Big Impact for Nature
passage.content: Looking after nature is everyone's job. Even small actions can make a big difference. At home, my family tries to reduce waste. We always separate our rubbish for recycling – plastic, paper, and glass go into different bins. We also try to reuse things, like old plastic containers for storage. When we go shopping, we bring our own reusable bags instead of taking new plastic ones. This helps reduce plastic pollution. We also save water by turning off the tap when brushing our teeth and taking shorter showers. In our garden, we plant flowers and small trees to help the local environment. These simple habits help protect our beautiful planet for the future.

questions.stemText: What is the main idea of the text?
options: Recycling is the only way to help nature.
Small actions can make a big difference in looking after nature.
Planting trees is the most important thing.
The writer's family uses a lot of plastic.

questions.stemText: What does the family do with their rubbish?
options: They throw it all away together.
They bury it in the garden.

questions.stemText: What do they reuse for storage?
What do they bring when they go shopping?
How do they save water?
options: By turning off the tap and taking shorter showers

questions.stemText: What does 'reduce waste' mean?
options: To use less and throw away less

questions.stemText: What do they plant in their garden?
Why are these habits important?
options: To make the house look nice
To protect our beautiful planet for the future

lessons.title: Local News: New Park Opens!
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners understand a simple news story. They will practice identifying key facts like who, what, when, and where, and understanding the main event.

sections.heading: Identifying Key Facts in a News Story
sections.content: News stories focus on facts. Look for the '5 Ws and 1 H': Who (was involved?), What (happened?), When (did it happen?), Where (did it happen?), Why (did it happen?), and How (did it happen?). These are the most important pieces of information.

sections.heading: Understanding the Main Event
sections.content: The first paragraph of a news story often summarizes the main event. Read this part carefully to get the overall picture. Then, the rest of the story gives more details. Try to identify the single most important thing that happened.

sections.heading: Vocabulary for News
sections.content: Words like 'report,' 'event,' 'official,' 'celebration,' 'community,' 'mayor,' 'project,' 'benefit,' 'open' are common in news texts. If you read 'the mayor cut the ribbon,' you know an important person performed an official opening ceremony.

passage.title: New Community Park Opens in District 7
passage.content: Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam – Yesterday, a brand new community park officially opened in District 7. The opening ceremony took place at 9 AM and was attended by local residents, students, and city officials, including Mayor Tran Van. The new park, named 'Green Oasis Park,' has a large playground for children, exercise equipment for adults, and many beautiful trees and flowers. The project took two years to complete and cost 5 billion VND. Mayor Tran Van said, 'This park will be a wonderful place for families to relax and for everyone to enjoy nature in the city.' The park is now open to the public every day from 6 AM to 9 PM, offering a green space for the whole community.

questions.stemText: What is the main news story about?
Where did this event take place?
Who attended the opening ceremony?
options: Local residents, students, and city officials

questions.stemText: What is the name of the new park?
What does the new park have for children?
What does 'officially opened' mean?
options: It was opened with a formal ceremony.
It was opened for a short time.

questions.stemText: How long did the park project take to complete?
What did Mayor Tran Van say the park would be?
options: A wonderful place for families to relax and enjoy nature

lessons.title: Learning to Play the Guitar
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners understand the process of learning a new skill. They will practice identifying motivations, challenges, and successes in learning.

sections.heading: Understanding the Learning Process
sections.content: When reading about learning a new skill, look for why someone started, what steps they took, what difficulties they faced, and what progress they made. This shows the journey of learning. Pay attention to words that describe effort and improvement.

sections.heading: Identifying Challenges and Successes
sections.content: Learning is rarely easy. Texts often mention challenges (e.g., 'difficult,' 'takes time,' 'frustrating') and successes (e.g., 'can play now,' 'feel proud,' 'improving'). Recognizing these helps you understand the full experience of learning. Connect problems to solutions or perseverance.

sections.heading: Vocabulary for Learning Skills
sections.content: Words like 'skill,' 'learn,' 'practice,' 'lesson,' 'improve,' 'difficult,' 'easy,' 'progress,' 'master,' 'instrument' are common. If you read 'my fingers hurt at first,' you can infer that playing a musical instrument can be physically challenging at the beginning.

passage.title: My Journey to Play the Guitar
passage.content: Last year, I decided to learn a new skill: playing the guitar. I always loved music and wanted to play my favorite songs. First, I bought a basic guitar and found some free online lessons. It was very difficult at the beginning! My fingers hurt, and it was hard to make the right sounds. I practiced for 30 minutes every day after school. My teacher, Mr. Nam, also gave me some tips. Slowly, I started to improve. After a few months, I could play simple songs. Now, I can play many songs, and I even write some of my own music. It takes a lot of patience and practice, but it's very rewarding. I feel proud when I can play a beautiful melody. Learning the guitar has brought so much joy to my life.

questions.stemText: What new skill did the writer decide to learn?
Why did the writer want to learn this skill?
options: Because they loved music and wanted to play favorite songs

questions.stemText: What was one difficulty the writer faced at the beginning?
options: Their fingers hurt, and it was hard to make right sounds.

questions.stemText: How often did the writer practice?
Who gave the writer some tips?
What does 'rewarding' mean in the text?
options: Making you feel happy and satisfied because of effort

questions.stemText: What can the writer do now after a few months?
options: Play many songs and write some of their own music

questions.stemText: How does learning the guitar make the writer feel?
